g.text: RPF failure — the packet arrived on an interface that is not the route back to the source

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reverse-path-forwarding check — a PROCEDURE that reads RIGHT TO LEFT. # # GENRE: `flowchart`, and it was `block` until this release. What the figure IS # never changed — a chain of stages, one decision, two terminal outcomes — but # under `block` the roles were carried by `shape=`: a diamond MEANT "decision" # and a rounded box MEANT "outcome", to a reader who had learned that. Shape is # presentation (`MEANING-RECOVERY-SOURCE`) and a convention has to be learned, while a word is read, # so those facts were asserted by nothing a reading agent could recover. Under # `flowchart` they are the keywords `process`, `decision` and `terminator`, the # geometry DERIVES from the role (box, diamond, rounded), and the figure states # what each stage is instead of drawing a hint at it (`DOMAIN-CONVENTION-DIRECTIVES`). # # THE PRICE, STATED: genre `flowchart` is EXPERIMENTAL — outside the # v0.1 conformance surface, so it may change or be withdrawn in a later `0.x`, # where `block` is normative. The declared version does NOT move: `flowchart` # has been dispatchable under `figdown 0.1` since the genre existed, and `edge` # is its connector word at this version (`flowline` is the 0.2 spelling and a # line error here). The four demonstrators below are genre-independent and all # four still execute — which is the only reason the trade was payable. # # What this figure probes: four constructs that had no demonstrator anywhere in # the corpus before 0.1. They are gathered into one small document on # purpose — a capability needs A demonstrator, not a document of its own. # # 1. `flow left` — the reverse direction. Twelve figures in this corpus use # `flow right` and twelve use `flow down`; `left` and `up` # had none, so half of the enum was untested by any figure. # 2. `\"` escape — a literal double quote INSIDE a quoted label. # 3. `#` inside a — a `[...]` region is verbatim (`VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE`): the # bracketed comment mark loses its meaning inside one, so an edge # edge label label may carry a `#` without quoting or escaping it. # 4. a NEGATIVE — `at=` is canvas px and the origin is not a wall. A pin may # `at=` pin sit at a negative coordinate; the canvas still starts at # (0,0) because it grows right and down only, so what the # negative value spends is the margin already above the # content — and no more than that. See the pin's own note. # # The subject fits the direction: an RPF check runs BACKWARDS along the path a # packet arrived on, so a figure that reads right to left is the honest layout, # not a stunt. That is the test for `flow left` in real use — if reversing the # reading order does not say something about the subject, use `flow right`. figdown 0.1 flowchart title "RPF check on a multicast join"
class fail "RPF failure — the packet arrived on an interface that is not the route back to the source" stroke=#b91c1c style=dashed
# The source is on the RIGHT because the check walks back TOWARDS it. It is an # `external`, not a `terminator`: the packet's origin is outside this procedure # and this figure does not describe it, so the edge simply ends open at a label. external src "from 198.51.100.7" # `\n` (a line break) and `\\` (a literal backslash) are the other two escapes # the grammar defines — core §11 lists exactly three, and all three are in this # file. The interface filter is a regex, which is where a backslash occurs # naturally in a network figure rather than as a demonstration of itself. # # NO `shape=` KEY SURVIVES THE CONVERSION, on purpose: the role supplies the # geometry, and re-stating it would put the drawing back in the author's hands # where the word already decides it. One visible delta and it is the honest one # — the ingress stage used to be drawn `shape=rounded` and now draws as a plain # box, because that is what `process` derives. The rounded corner was never # meaning; `terminator` (accept, drop) is where rounded means "this is where the # procedure ends", and those two still draw rounded because their ROLE says so. process rx "Ingress ge-0/0/1\nfilter ge-0/0/\\d+" process lookup "Unicast RIB lookup" # The escape `\"` puts a literal double quote inside a quoted label. The label # is one token to the parser either way — the quotes delimit it, the backslash # says "this quote is data". decision verdict "Arrived on the \"upstream\" interface?" terminator accept "Accept and forward" terminator drop "Drop (RPF fail)" class=fail
# `#` inside a bracketed edge label. Before `VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE` this needed quoting, because # the comment scanner ran before the label scanner and ate the rest of the line; # the ruling made a verbatim region protect EVERY mark, not just the one that # earned the rule. So `[VRF #7]` is six characters of label, not a comment. edge src -[VRF #7]-> rx edge rx -> lookup edge lookup -[next-hop ge-0/0/1]-> verdict edge verdict -[yes]-> accept edge verdict -[no]-> drop class=fail
# NO layout zone, on purpose (maintainer review). This figure # spent its whole life hand-tuned — `flow left`, a `rank`, and the corpus's # only negative-coordinate `pin` — and the maintainer compared the tuned # drawing against the genre's own default and ruled the default better: a # top-down flowchart with the verdict fanning to its two outcomes is the # drawing every reader already knows how to read. So the tuning went, which # is itself the demonstration `GUI-WRITEBACK-STRUCTURE` makes: strip the layout zone and the figure # says the same thing — here the stripped form is not merely equivalent but # preferred. The negative-coordinate findings that used to live beside the # pin (what `at=` does and does not do to the canvas) moved to # examples/patterns/block-c.fd, whose side-cache lift is a subject that # actually wants a negative coordinate, instead of riding a figure that no # longer needs one.
